Source: the Memory-R1 paper (`library/llm/memory/agent/`) and its note. I checked each number below against the paper's markdown tables.

**1. Training questions: 152.** The authors take LoCoMo, leave out its adversarial subset and split the rest 1:1:8. That gives 152 training, 81 validation and 1,307 test questions ([p. 5, §4.1](http://pdf.invalid/llm/memory/agent/Memory-R1.%20Enhancing%20Large%20Language%20Model%20Agents%20to%20Manage%20and%20Utilize%20Memories%20via%20Reinforcement.pdf?dest=subsection.4.1&page=5)). The abstract also mentions "only 152 training QA pairs" ([p. 1](http://pdf.invalid/llm/memory/agent/Memory-R1.%20Enhancing%20Large%20Language%20Model%20Agents%20to%20Manage%20and%20Utilize%20Memories%20via%20Reinforcement.pdf?page=1&search=With%20only%20152%20training%20QA%20pairs)).

**2. Against Mem0 on LLaMA-3.1-8B (LoCoMo, overall).** The scores come from [p. 5, Table 1](http://pdf.invalid/llm/memory/agent/Memory-R1.%20Enhancing%20Large%20Language%20Model%20Agents%20to%20Manage%20and%20Utilize%20Memories%20via%20Reinforcement.pdf?dest=table.1&page=5):

| Method | F1 | BLEU-1 | LLM judge (J) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mem0 | 30.41 | 22.22 | 45.68 |
| Memory-R1-PPO | 41.05 | 32.91 | 57.54 |
| Memory-R1-GRPO | 45.02 | 37.51 | 62.74 |

- **The relative gains don't match the table.** The introduction says GRPO beats Mem0 by 28% in F1, 34% in BLEU-1 and 30% in J ([p. 2](http://pdf.invalid/llm/memory/agent/Memory-R1.%20Enhancing%20Large%20Language%20Model%20Agents%20to%20Manage%20and%20Utilize%20Memories%20via%20Reinforcement.pdf?dest=section.1&page=2&search=relative%20improvements)). Table 1 itself gives +48%, +69% and +37%. The text probably comes from an earlier version of the paper; I didn't check this against the PDF.
- **Mem0 here is the authors' own re-run.** They re-implemented every baseline on the 8B backbone, so Mem0 scores much lower here than in its own paper ([p. 5](http://pdf.invalid/llm/memory/agent/Memory-R1.%20Enhancing%20Large%20Language%20Model%20Agents%20to%20Manage%20and%20Utilize%20Memories%20via%20Reinforcement.pdf?dest=subsection.4.1&page=5)).
- **The fine-tuned baseline is close behind.** Memory-SFT (same setup, trained on GPT-5 trajectories instead of with RL) reaches J 58.76, about 4 points under GRPO (p. 5, Table 1).

**3. LongMemEval: the gain is small.** The model is trained only on LoCoMo and tested on LongMemEval without further training. Scores below are F1 / BLEU-1 / J from [p. 17, Table 5](http://pdf.invalid/llm/memory/agent/Memory-R1.%20Enhancing%20Large%20Language%20Model%20Agents%20to%20Manage%20and%20Utilize%20Memories%20via%20Reinforcement.pdf?dest=table.5&page=17):

| Backbone | Memory-R1-GRPO | Best baseline | Mem0 |
|---|---|---|---|
| LLaMA-3.1-8B | 45.2 / 39.3 / 55.4 | Memory-SFT 43.9 / 36.7 / 54.8 | 31.4 / 21.7 / 41.2 |
| Qwen-2.5-7B | 46.7 / 41.1 / 57.8 | A-Mem 41.6 / 36.6 / 54.8 (Memory-SFT also 54.8 J) | 38.4 / 34.5 / 46.8 |

- **Against the strongest baseline:** +0.6 J on LLaMA and +3.0 J on Qwen.
- **Against Mem0:** +14.2 J on LLaMA and +11.0 J on Qwen.
- **PPO on Qwen** (J 47.4) falls below A-Mem.
- **No spread is reported.** The paper gives no variance across seeds, so the +0.6 on LLaMA could be noise.
- **The text oversells it.** It calls this "consistent improvements" ([p. 6, §4.3](http://pdf.invalid/llm/memory/agent/Memory-R1.%20Enhancing%20Large%20Language%20Model%20Agents%20to%20Manage%20and%20Utilize%20Memories%20via%20Reinforcement.pdf?dest=subsection.4.3&page=6)), which the numbers don't really support.

One problem with the paper's note: its digest compares the LongMemEval result to A-Mem on LLaMA (55.4 vs 54.2). The strongest LLaMA baseline is actually Memory-SFT at 54.8. I haven't edited the note; I can correct it if you like.

No files changed, so there's nothing to commit.
